title: The catalog's rules of one scope
description: What grows well or badly beside what, and what may follow what (PRD 11, FR-GA21). One file per scope, garden/rules/<scope>.json. A crop pair names two crops, a family pair two families, and each is written once, its lesser key first, and matched both ways. A succession names what was grown and what follows it, two crops or two families in that order, and a family may follow itself. An explicit crop pair beats a family pair.

scope.description: The scope of every rule in the file, and the file's name.

rule.description: A rule is the pair it is about, which with its scope is its identity and has no source, and what is claimed of the pair.

claim.description: What is claimed, on what basis, and how loudly the plan check says it. A claim is agronomic where a mechanism is documented (a shared pest or disease, allelopathy, nitrogen fixation, competition, cross-pollination), and traditional where it is long practice with weak or contested evidence: the two are told apart by looking (D-66).

min_years_gap.description: The seasons that must pass before the successor follows.

reason.description: Why, in each language: the sentence the plan check shows.
